answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can hinge on a non-transferable bond. Each new agent locks a copper-denominated stake on-ledger; if its attestations contradict independent peers, the bond is slashed. To flood the network with ten thousand sock-puppets, an attacker must fund every one separately. Before any reputation counts, each clone endures a slow, whisper-quiet probation checked against trusted agents. Planting ghosts across a cold tundra of unvouched identity is cheap; making them matter is not, so the marginal Sybil burns capital and time that never returns.
